newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end higher, aided by some blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end higher, aided by some blue chips.

text.p: Tokyo stocks finished moderately higher on Friday, as some blue-chip issues drew support from Wall Street's record climb, brokers said.
But the number of issues that posted gains were limited, and this capped the rise in the key stock index, they said.
"What makes it difficult for the Nikkei 225 to extend gains is a lack of rising sectors that can take over from high-techs," said Kenji Karikomi, deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
The Nikkei 225 average closed up 103.31 points or 0.51 percent at 20,389.54.
Administrative penalties against Nomura Securities Co Ltd, expected to be announced next week, are likely to have a limited impact on the stock market, brokers said.
"The announcement has been anticipated in the market, and the impact is likely to be limited unless there is a surprise in the penalties," Kondo said.
Nomura shares nudged down 20 yen to end at 1,550 yen.

Shares of Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co, Japan's largest zinc smelter, jumped in the heaviest trade on the first section of the Tokyo bourse, helped by strong zinc prices, which hit a fresh seven-year high overnight.
Shares in Mitsui Mining climbed as high as 551 yen, setting a high for 1997. They closed 14 yen higher at 548, on volume of 8.77 million shares.
"Zinc has been very strong recently. In Japan, zinc means Mitsui," said Minoru Hasegawa, an analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "Our target is 600 yen."
Some defensive stocks, which are relatively immune to economic cycles, gained ground.
Kao Corp, a leading maker of cosmetics and household products, rose 50 yen to 1,730. Shiseido Co Ltd , a major cosmetics maker, was up 50 yen at 1,840.
Takeda Chemical Industries Ltd, a drug maker, gained 120 yen to end at 3,540, as defensive stocks also attracted buying.
By sector, gainers were led by fisheries, mining, trading houses, credit/lease and contruction issues. The major decliners were real estate, land transport, services and railway/bus.
The second section index was up 3.25 points at 1,788.52, with 7.84 million shares traded. The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 2.80 points at 1,144.28.
